through the Key Vault firewall (public endpoint on, default action Deny, trusted Azure services bypass).

Agents Behind the Wall - diagram 02 of 13 - generated by docs/diagrams/build_diagrams.py
13 network-stage zones the Foundry template references as existing (the 14th, APIM's, is below)
Also in use: the APIM endpoint zone and the internal Container Apps zone
- snet-agent has no NAT gateway and no default outbound access: the agent runtime has no internet
path. It reaches APIM through a private endpoint and the private MCP at its internal name.
- Storage, Cosmos DB and AI Search accept no public traffic and no keys. The only way to data is a
private endpoint, with an on-behalf-of token.
- All VNet egress leaves through one NAT address, the only address on the Key Vault firewall. The
APIM NSG allows three outbound destinations on 443; the jump-box NSG admits only Bastion and
1. A client calls the APIM public gateway with a bearer token. Wall 1 (APIM) judges every call
2. The agent runtime has no internet path, so it reaches the same gateway through the APIM
3. APIM's backend calls leave through its outbound VNet integration in snet-apim.
4. They stay inside the VNet to the MCP apps in the internal Container Apps environment
5. The private MCP is called straight from the agent subnet at its internal name. It is never
behind APIM, so Wall 1 and the kill switch do not apply to it.
6. After the on-behalf-of exchange, the MCP servers reach Storage, Cosmos DB and AI
Search through private endpoints. Private DNS answers with 10.42.1.x addresses.
7. Public hosts (Entra, Azure Monitor, the vendor mock) are reached through the NAT
gateway's one static address, from snet-mcp, snet-apim and snet-jump only.
8. The operator opens the VM in the Azure portal and connects through Bastion Developer.
9. Bastion reaches the VM on RDP 3389, the only inbound NSG rule. From the VM the
private names resolve to the private endpoints.
Direct to the private MCP's internal name: never behind APIM
